title: Provision S3 Encryption Configuration
scenario: Your platform team needs S3 Encryption Configuration for encrypting objects at rest with AES256. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).

focus.title: Complete the aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.

hints.why: S3 is usually the first shared service in an AWS configuration. Bucket settings, versioning, encryption and public-access blocks are common review findings.
hints.what: Complete the marked TODO in `main.tf`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration. Use the visible constraints as your checklist before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use S3 when you need durable object storage for assets, logs, backups or static content, and lock down access from the start.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work inside the single TODO region. Change one requirement at a time: add the named block, argument or reference, then run the tests. When a check fails, match its wording to the constraints and fix only the block it names.
